_comment: SEED / EXAMPLE — one illustrative output-quality case, here to demonstrate the evals/ dev-artifact convention (see skills/README.md), not a populated suite. Its expectations are grounded in write-readme's own documented house style; expected_output is a description of success, not a captured README. Choosing which skills to evaluate, how many cases, and running each case with and without the skill for the baseline delta (via Anthropic's skill-creator) is a workspace activity, left to whoever runs it — nothing here is committed as a benchmark result.

evals.prompt: Write a README for a new kirchDev CLI called envprism that manages per-environment configuration profiles.
evals.expected_output: A README.md in the kirchDev house style: a centered hero header, a one-line usage hook, feature bullets, and the standard closing sections — good enough that a reader reaches the install/run command within the first screen.
expectations: The output is a Markdown README, not prose describing one.
It opens with a centered hero header carrying an emoji and a bold tagline.
A one-liner code-snippet hook appears near the top.
Feature bullets use the house style's prescribed section emojis.
It ends with the standardized Versioning and License sections.
